page.layout: One page of running text in one column; at the foot a line of catchword, "Quo-" at the right. No margin notes, no running head beyond the printed title line at the top.

main_text.p: bili sagacitate ἡ ἀγχινοΐα mentis, aliud ex alio rite colligentis, percipiunt. Ac non tam oculis cernūt, quàm mente uident: sicut rectè monet Aristoteles in Problematis, cū adducit peruulgatum dictum: Νῆς ὀφθαλμὸς ἡ νῦς ἀνθρώπου. Idem de Morte: Delectationes, inquit, animæ sunt, cognoscere creatorem, considerare opera cœlorum, & sapientiam illius. Plutarchus ad priu-s Aristotelis, immò uulgi dictum alludens: Mens, ait, uidet, mens audit: reliqua surda cæcaq; sunt, & rationis indiga. In Commentario de Fortuna Alexandri.

Iam uerò, cum ij quos Iehouah alloquitur in hac oratione, etiam fidei luce illuminatos haberent mentis oculos, multo magis decebat eos opera Domini rite cō templari. Fide enim intelligimus, quid rerū Deus ille conditor & redemtor nobis-cum agat. Hebr. 11.
Quare longè aliter Dei opera hominibus intelligentibus, quàm brutis animalibus: fidelibus hominibus, quàm ceteri, qui sunt infideles, solent, spectanda & perpendenda sunt.

page.notes: Greek line after "dictum:" is printed as Νῆς ὀφθαλμὸς ... in the scan and is only partly legible; the word "ἀνθρώπου" and the Greek accents are doubtful, and the first Greek word may be misread. "ἡ ἀγχινοΐα" is doubtful. "Iehouah" and "Hebr. 11." are copied as printed. Last line of the page reads "Quo-" as catchword.
